Subject: Observability packaging: retention + tracing + advanced dashboards — savings scenarios and next steps

Hi James,

Thanks again for taking the demo last week — great to see Acme's use case around long-term session search and end-to-end trace correlation. As promised, I attached a short set of packaging scenarios that show how retention, tracing, and advanced dashboards can be bundled to meet your cost and SLA requirements.

Key highlights in the attached PDF:
- Baseline: pay-go retention with 30d trace window + standard dashboards (no commit)
- Optimized: 12-month commit for retention + continuous trace sampling + advanced dashboards included (saves ~28% vs baseline at your projected volumes)
- Hybrid: 6-month commitment + burst credits for surge retention + optional live trace export (saves ~16% with predictable capex)

Two quick asks so we can tighten numbers:
1) Can you confirm the 90th percentile token retention and peak tracing QPS for month 1 and month 6? (we used your numbers from the demo but want to validate)
2) Any internal constraints on SLA or audit log retention beyond standard 12 months?

I've cc'd Ben who will map the SOW and pricing table to the scenario you prefer. If it helps, we can propose a pilot: 3-month pilot with reduced dashboard seats and a one-time credit to cover onboarding instrumentation.

Attachments: Redwood_Obs_Pricing_Scenarios_v1.pdf, observability-pricing-breakdown.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon,

--

Appreciate the quick follow-up and materials. A couple of clarifying notes from our side:

- For month 1 we expect ~120M tokens/day and ~400 QPS for tracing spikes; by month 6 our plan is ~180M tokens/day with 800 QPS peaks.
- We need retained logs available for 18 months for compliance — SOC team flagged this.
- Procurement will want an annual commitment option but also wants to understand overage behavior and surge credits.

Two asks from procurement:
1) Can you provide a clear mapping of how the optimized and hybrid scenarios change the monthly invoice line items? (separate lines for retention storage, tracing ingests, dashboard seats, and surge credits)
2) What flexibility is there on a first-year concession — Acme is evaluating two vendors and would like a one-time onboarding credit and a pilot discount.

We can loop in Ben on the invoicing language.

Thanks,
James

James — looping in a price-able SOW and a sample invoice breakout. Quick summary below and attachments include a draft SOW (SOW_ACME_v2.pdf) and a spreadsheet that separates each billable line.

What we recommend based on your numbers and the 18-month retention requirement:
- Platform tier: Dedicated retention slab with 18-month archival path (monthly amortized storage line)
- Tracing: Continuous sampling for hot paths + tiered long-tail trace storage (ingest + storage lines separated)
- Dashboards: Advanced dashboards billed per seat, with 10 seats included in the pilot; extra seats add-on monthly

Commercial proposal (first-year):
- 12-month commit with soft ramp (monthly consumption floors for months 1–3 at 60% of target; full commit from month 4)
- Pilot concession: 50% off dashboard seats for months 1–3; one-time onboarding credit of $25k to cover instrumentation and playbook work
- Volume discount ladder: 10% at commit >= $150k/mo, 18% at commit >= $300k/mo

We can tighten language on overages: surge credits applied automatically for spikes above 120% of committed QPS (credits drawn from a pre-negotiated bucket); true overage billable at list but we aim for smoothing via credits.

Attachments: SOW_ACME_v2.pdf, observability-pricing-breakdown.xlsx

Ben — please confirm the discount math. Kimberly, can you confirm whether we can legally commit to the surge credit mechanism as written?

Thanks,

1) Can Redwood stretch to a one-time 20% total concession on the first-year committed amount in exchange for a 24-month notice-to-terminate clause (we can sign a clause that gives both parties 60 days notice after month 12)? This is the main ask that moves us from vendor selection -> exec approval.
2) We need a written exception for 18-month retention in our contract (standard Redwood policy says 12 months) and confirmation that the archived data is stored in the us-east-1 region.

If you can confirm both items, procurement will route the SOW for signatures this week.
